financing.summary: Epcon is a private, founder-owned company with no public debt, ratings or disclosed bank facilities, so most of its financing is not public. What is public: each company-owned community sits in its own single-member project LLC, the corporate arm buys and develops its own land in-house, and Epcon project LLCs have been filing SEC Form D notices since at least 2016; the nine notices opened for 2024 and 2025 are all small private debt placements ($250K to $2.7M each, one investor each, two placed by a small Ohio broker-dealer, Lincoln Douglas Investments). That pattern points to project-by-project private capital on top of undisclosed bank loans, not a programmatic land bank; no land banker, lot-option partner or link to Domain, Millrose, Kennedy Lewis or TPG Angelo Gordon was found. It is a plausible but small land-banking customer: only the roughly 600-home company-owned arm (six markets, about 18 active communities at the end of 2024, average price about $721K) is one counterparty, while the other half of the 1,269 ranked closings belongs to 60+ independent franchise builders who, per the franchise disclosure document, mostly buy raw ground and fund it with local bank or family-office acquisition and development loans that Epcon does not provide.
financing.land_strategy: Owns and develops (not land-light, as far as public sources show). The affiliates buy raw land and develop lots themselves through single-member project LLCs; a May 2025 Columbus job advert for a Land Development Project Manager describes in-house lot delivery. No owned/optioned split or target is published. The franchise disclosure document says most franchisees also buy raw ground rather than finished lots.

lots.source_title: 2025 Franchise Disclosure Document, Item 20 (as reproduced by FDD Ninja)
lots.note: No lot counts are public. Closest public proxies: 18 company-owned communities selling at the end of 2024 (18 at the start; 20 at the start of 2022), 23 company-owned communities with closings during 2024, and six new company-owned communities projected for 2025 (three in Georgia, three in Indiana, in the part of the table that was readable). The FDD puts cumulative company-owned development at 128 communities and about 11,006 homes since 1986 including 2025 estimates.

joint_ventures.description: The franchisor's listed parent companies are EC Franchising, LLC, Epcon JV LLC and Epcon Holding LLC, all at the Dublin headquarters. The 'JV' holding entity and the 'EC New Vision' homebuilding affiliates set up from June 2018 suggest a restructured ownership or capital arrangement, but no outside partner is named anywhere public.
joint_ventures.source_title: 2025 Franchise Disclosure Document, Item 1 (as reproduced by FDD Ninja)
joint_ventures.note: Entity names and dates are from the FDD; the reading that they reflect an outside capital partner is an inference and may be wrong (they may simply be founder holding companies).

key_metrics.source_title: 2025 Franchise Disclosure Document, auditor's report on Epcon Communities Franchising, LLC (as reproduced by FDD Ninja)

gaps: Bank lenders, revolver or construction/A&D facilities of the homebuilding affiliates: not publicly disclosed (private company). The franchisor's audited statements mention cash at two unnamed financial institutions.
Lot counts (owned, optioned, years of supply): not publicly disclosed.

Land banker or lot-option partner: none found in public sources. A dedicated search for Epcon with Millrose, Kennedy Lewis, TPG Angelo Gordon or Domain could not be run because the swarm's shared web-search allowance was exhausted; nothing in the sources opened mentions any of them.

Identity of the investors in the Form D debt placements, and the rate, maturity and security of that debt: not disclosed (Form D does not require it). The placements could be private investor notes, mezzanine loans or seller notes; the filings do not say.

Seven more Epcon project LLCs appear as EDGAR filers (Andrews Chapel and Wesley Chapel, 2016; Westfield, Lochmere, Carr Farms, Glenshire and Oak Grove, about 2021 to 2023) but their notices were not opened; the debt table covers 2024 and 2025 only and is not a total of project debt.

Total debt, cash, liquidity, leverage and revenue of the homebuilding entities: not publicly disclosed. Only the franchisor (Epcon Communities Franchising, LLC) has audited statements in the FDD, and those were not read in full; they show non-interest-bearing advances from the franchisor to the homebuilding affiliate with no stated maturity (amount not captured).

Capital raising: a search-result summary of a Builder article (not openable, 403) said the CEO described raising more capital for land acquisition and development; no amount, date or source of capital is public.

M&A: no acquisition, sale or merger involving Epcon in 2025 or 2026 was found in the sources opened; growth has come from new franchise signings (Dayton, Greenville and Chicagoland/Quad Cities builders in 2025) and from the 2021 to 2022 organic entries into Indianapolis, Atlanta and Nashville. A dedicated M&A search could not be run (search allowance exhausted).

The FDD facts come from a third-party reproduction of the April 11, 2025 Franchise Disclosure Document (fdd.ninja), not the state-registry copy, so they are tagged Reported; the 2026 FDD was not found.
